concerns: All sampled filter examples repeat just four sentences except service numbers; classify examples likewise repeat four sentences except ticket numbers. This measures template recognition more than broad semantic generalization.
Development and held-out examples visibly share exact language templates. Row separation alone does not prevent template leakage; generalization claims need distinct held-out phrasing and scenarios.
Extract inputs use rigid labeled fields and explicit missingness phrases; there are no sampled conflicting dates/owners, indirect references, missing titles or freeform task descriptions.
Sampled labels are clear, but the set lacks negation, mixed positive/negative feedback, hypothetical failures, recovered outages and ambiguous feature-versus-bug cases.
Numbers embedded in IDs and texts may permit shortcuts in a synthetic dataset. Labels here were inferred exclusively from the substantive input language.
ambiguities: Minor extraction boundary convention: interpret final sentence periods as punctuation rather than part of title/owner/date. No material semantic label ambiguities in these 50 examples.
